subject: Dedicated capacity token-rate guarantees and measurement methodology

Subject: Dedicated capacity: token-rate guarantees and measurement methodology

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re interested in a Dedicated GPU pool for our inference traffic and need to understand the guarantee you can commit to around token-rate and latency. Two things we need answered before procurement:

1) What specific token/sec (and/or requests/sec) guarantees do you provide for a reserved commit (e.g., 1k T/s sustained, 5k T/s burst)?
2) How do you measure that in acceptance testing? What measurement methodology and tooling do you require from our side (synthetic driver, replay, length distributions, KV/cache warm-up)?
3) If you miss the guarantee, what credit/discount mechanisms are available?

We also have some variability in prompt length and heavy prefix caching benefits for our workload — so please describe how you account for warm cache vs cold-start in the acceptance window.

Can you reply with the technical acceptance steps and a proposed commercial fallback? We’d like to bake this into a PO/commit.

Best,
Jose
Director, Procurement
MegaCorp

Hi Jose — thanks for the clear list. I’ll summarize the high level here and loop in Aditya for the measurement plan + Stephanie on the commercial fallback.

High-level answers:
- We provide commitments expressed as sustained tokens/sec (T/s) for the committed GPU pool plus short burst allowance tied to unused headroom. We publish both sustained T/s and p95 latency targets for expected prompt distributions.
- Acceptance testing is a joint runbook: a 48-hour measurement window using both replay (your production traces scrubbed) and a synthetic driver that mimics your length distribution and concurrency. We measure sustained T/s over rolling 5-minute windows and verify p95/p99 latency while the KV cache is warmed to steady-state.
- If targets are missed we offer monetary credits based on the severity and duration of the miss; Stephanie will propose specific bands linked to commit size.

Action items:
- Aditya: can you attach the measurement CSV and a short checklist for the PoC run?
- Jose: please share one day of representative traces (scrubbed) and expected QPS pattern. We can take them as replay or build the synthetic waveform.

I’m available for a short call tomorrow to walk through the runbook.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Hi Jose, quick technical note on the measurement methodology we recommend and why we report tokens/sec vs requests/sec: 

1) Tokens/sec vs requests/sec:
   - Tokens/sec (T/s) is the most stable unit for GPU-based inference because costs and GPU utilization correlate with output token work and KV-cache behavior. Requests/sec varies heavily with prompt length. We report both T/s and R/s during acceptance, but guarantees are expressed primarily in T/s with accompanying latency SLOs.

2) Key measurement concepts:
   - Warm vs cold cache: acceptance should include a warm-up phase (we recommend 2–6 hours of representative traffic or a replay warm-up) to bring KV caches and shared prefix caches to steady-state. Final verification is performed after warm-up.
   - Rolling measurement windows: sustained T/s is validated on rolling 5-minute windows across a 48-hour acceptance window; we look for at least 95% of windows meeting the committed T/s.
   - Latency targets: p95/p99 measured at the same windows. We include both generation latency (server-side) and end-to-end token emission time for streaming flows.
   - Burst handling: we allow for short bursts (typically up to 2x sustained for <2 minutes) as a courtesy; sustained billing and guarantees use the sustained band only.

3) Test harness & tooling:
   - We can run two parallel harnesses: (a) replay of scrubbed production traces you provide (recommended) and (b) synthetic driver that reproduces your prompt length distribution and concurrency envelope.
   - Measurement artifacts: per-request sample CSV (ts, prompt_len, response_tokens, latency_ms), aggregate T/s timeseries, and a final verification report. I’ve attached "throughput-test-plan.csv" with the fields we need for the replay and a checklist for KV warm-up.

4) Acceptance criteria example (for illustration):
   - Sustained: 2,000 T/s (rolling 5m) with >=95% of 5m windows meeting target over 48 hours.
   - Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for baseline prompt distribution.

If you’re OK with the approach I’ll run an initial dry-run in our staging cluster and share the scripts/trackers.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal SRE - Inference Platform, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Hi Jose — looping in the commercial terms and proposed credit structure we typically use for Dedicated commitments. Attached I’ve included a short SLA draft (redwood-dedicated-sla-draft.pdf) you can review. Highlights below: 

Commercial proposal (illustrative, final bands depend on commit size):
- Reserved commit tiers: Small (500–2k T/s), Mid (2k–10k T/s), Large (>10k T/s). Pricing scales per T/s with volume discount.
- Discount structure: 10% off list at Small on 12-mo commit, 18% for Mid, 25% for Large (examples).
- Credits for underperformance: If sustained T/s or p95 latency falls short for >4 consecutive hours during the acceptance window or during a calendar month, we issue pro-rata service credits up to 30% of that month’s commit bill for sustained misses; transient blips covered by a 1 hour tolerance.

Acceptance & billing flow:
1) PoC / acceptance window (48h) — PASS/FAIL on the runbook. If PASS, commit is activated and billing starts on day 1 of production.
2) If FAILED, customer may choose: (a) extended remediation + re-test (no charge), (b) lower-commit band + adjusted pricing, or (c) termination with full refund of setup fees.

Contract language we recommend adding: a clear definition of measurement artifacts, the rolling window logic, and an agreed list of scripts/trace files. We also ask for a single point of contact on client side for the replay.

Next steps I propose:
- Jose: confirm the desired commit tier (ballpark T/s) so we can price and slot capacity.
- Ava/Aditya: schedule the 48h PoC; Aditya to share the harness and expected data format.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Commercials & Partnerships, Redwood Inference
